newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices were mixed on Thursday in a slow market that was difficult to gauge due to volatility in the energy complex, traders said.
"There were hardly any inquiries, ships or oil moving," said one West Coast trader.
In Los Angeles, spot 380 CST edged up $1 to between $107 and $108 a tonne, with 180 CST rising $2 to $115/116 in thin talk.
"There's been a lot of volatility in the market, with the Far East prices being up and down the past few days and people starting to switch over to heating oil," said one trader.
Slow trade also plagued the East Coast, where spot New York Harbor 380 CST dipped $1 to $117/119 a tonne and 180 CST was quoted $122/124.
One East Coast trader said that small deals were scarce, butsuppliers were competing with each other for bigger parcels -- 1,000 and 1,500 tonnes -- to try to catch current high prices.
Norfolk traded at a slight premium to the harbor.
On the Gulf Coast, Houston values remained steady amid low supply levels and weak demand, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
